klappen_headline: Three generations. A broken oath. A coalfield that falls silent.
klappentext:
Voßlohe, 1905: in the great strike the young hewer Wilhelm Kortmann breaks the solidarity – he betrays his butty to save his own family, and rises. On that betrayal everything the family later has is built.

Across three generations the fault is hauled up with the coal – through war, dictatorship, forced labour and the dying of the pits – until in 1989, as the last shift closes the shaft, his granddaughter Marga must decide what a century of silence is worth.
praemisse: Across a century, a miners' family in Germany's Ruhr valley is bound to a colliery that feeds and owns them. When the grandfather breaks the solidarity of the great 1905 strike to save his children and ruins a comrade for it, he lays a fault that is hauled up with the coal: through war, dictatorship, forced labour, reconstruction and the dying of the pits, until the last shift closes the shaft in 1989 - and the third generation must decide whether an inherited betrayal is buried or named. The title carries a triple meaning: the work shift, the geological seam, the social class.
